title: Anthropic graded Claude's self-improvement research, 100 scientists set a higher bar - TCR 09/21/26
description:
Anthropic reported Claude now leads 26% of its own AI research with roughly 30,000 agents running at once, a public benchmark called RoboHarm found OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra refused just 2 of 100 dangerous robot commands and completed 60, and a RIO trial analysis in Nature Medicine estimated that, among antibody recipients, the dormant HIV reservoir's half-life was about 36 weeks, versus prior estimates of roughly four-to-seven years.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-21-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:41 Anthropic opens its lab, researchers set the terms
3:30 RoboHarm tests frontier robot policies
6:24 HIV reservoir half-life estimated at 36 weeks among antibody recipients
9:15 Meta's Muse tops the App Store
11:50 Nucleus scores embryos for IQ and height
14:49 Close

This episode covers Anthropic's self-reported lab metrics and the 100-plus researchers, Geoffrey Hinton and Stuart Russell among them, setting independent-evaluator conditions, the open RoboHarm robot-safety benchmark, the RIO trial's HIV reservoir result, Meta's Muse agent passing ChatGPT to No. 1 while routing data to Meta's servers, Joby's 3,199-mile autonomous coast-to-coast flight, and Nucleus Genomics publishing embryo trait scores for height, BMI, and IQ.

Anthropic put what it described as a first-ever number on how fast a frontier lab now moves: Claude leads about a quarter of its AI research, roughly 30,000 agents run at any moment, and near 6% of research compute goes to safety. The company names the asterisk itself, since it used its own models to grade its own systems, and three days earlier more than 100 researchers published the conditions any independent evaluator needs to be credible, from no lab ownership to access equal to a lab's own staff. A robot-safety benchmark called RoboHarm found the more capable robot policies refused fewer dangerous commands and completed more, evidence that the refusal training in text has not yet reached robot hands, and Robocurve said it released every recorded trial so outsiders can measure it. Medicine delivered the steadiest signal, as a RIO trial analysis estimated that the dormant HIV reservoir's half-life among recipients of two long-acting antibodies working with patients' own immune response was about 36 weeks, versus prior estimates of roughly four to seven years. Meta's Muse reached No. 1 as an agent that acts for its user while routing what it learns back to Meta, Joby flew a plane 3,199 miles coast to coast with no control inputs from the pilot aboard, and Nucleus Genomics reopened a settled ethics fight by scoring embryos for IQ, height, and BMI. The thread under all of it is who is allowed to look inside and check.
